note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Text-based vs visual-based retrieval gaps -> Unveil's visual-textual teacher and distilled visual-only student

nodes.name: OCR pipelines are costly and lossy
nodes.description: Traditional OCR-then-text retrieval (BM25, DPR) adds computational overhead, introduces recognition errors, and misses crucial visual context.

nodes.name: Visual methods weak on text-rich content
nodes.description: Parsing-free visual retrievers (e.g. DSE, VisRAG) outperform text-based methods in visual-rich scenarios but struggle with semantic details in text-rich scenarios such as web-page retrieval.

nodes.name: Complementary strengths
nodes.description: Text-based methods model linguistic semantics but overlook layout and graphics, while purely visual methods preserve visual context but struggle with fine-grained language understanding.

nodes.name: Visual-textual teacher model
nodes.description: Unveil's visual-textual dual-encoder model feeds the VLM the document image plus its OCR text (prompt ' What is shown in this image?') and uses the end-of-sequence token embedding as representation.

nodes.name: Hybrid score merging is not enough
nodes.description: Hybrid models combining text-based and visual-based scores give intermediate results, can fall below text-based models alone in web-page retrieval, and cost inference from both models.

nodes.name: Teacher beats all baselines
nodes.description: The Unveil visual-textual model consistently achieves the highest performance across all retrieval scenarios, surpassing text-based, visual-based and hybrid methods.

nodes.name: Distillation design
nodes.description: The visual-only student is trained with representation alignment, soft label distillation from the teacher's score distribution, and adaptive re-weighting that upweights documents with high teacher-student KL divergence, under Ltotal = sum w_i (L_align + L_soft).

nodes.name: Distilled student rivals teacher without OCR
nodes.description: The distilled visual-only Unveil exceeds text-based and visual-based baselines and approaches the teacher's performance while requiring no text input at inference.

nodes.name: Every distillation component helps
nodes.description: Ablation shows removing adaptive re-weighting, representation alignment or soft-label distillation each degrades performance, with removing representation alignment causing significant degradation.

nodes.name: Distillation aligns embeddings
nodes.description: t-SNE of 200 ChartQA documents shows student representations become much more aligned with the teacher's after distillation and cosine similarity between them increases.

nodes.name: Text length helps then saturates
nodes.description: Teacher performance improves as input OCR text length grows from 0 to 3096, with a large jump from 0 to 512 and diminishing gains from 2048 to 3096, but longer text raises inference cost.

evidence: Sec 5 Impact of Text Length, Table 4

isolated_nodes.name: BM25 beats BGE-Large on visual docs
isolated_nodes.description: BM25 outperforms the dense BGE-Large retriever on visual documents because their text is fragmented and semantically incoherent, favoring string matching.

isolated_nodes.name: Experimental setup
isolated_nodes.description: Both teacher and student are initialized from MiniCPM-V 2.0 and fine-tuned with in-batch negatives for two epochs (batch size 16, lr 2e-5, 8 A100 80GB GPUs), evaluated on 12 datasets with Recall@10 and MRR@10.

isolated_nodes.name: Two inference modes
isolated_nodes.description: Unveil offers a Visual-Textual mode with OCR plus images for best precision and a Visual-Only mode without OCR that significantly reduces computational overhead.

structural_reasoning: Argument runs from complementary weaknesses of text-based and visual-based retrieval to the visual-textual teacher, the distillation scheme, and supporting empirical analyses.
